name: Mayans
hook: Pyramids, a Long Count calendar and a jaguar god: the Maya of Mexico and Central America.

facts.label: Tikal
facts.statement: Tikal, with temples and pyramids in a Guatemalan rainforest, has the tallest surviving Mayan building.

facts.label: Chichen Itza
facts.statement: Chichen Itza is on the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico; its El Castillo pyramid was dedicated to the serpent god Kukulkan.

facts.label: Copan
facts.statement: Copan, in Honduras near the Guatemalan border, was a Classic-period Maya city where 16 kings ruled from about 400 to 800 A.D.

facts.label: the Long Count
facts.statement: The Maya kept a Long Count calendar that begins in 3114 B.C., the era when the Sumerians settled Ur.

facts.label: the jaguar
facts.statement: The Maya revered the jaguar, Panthera onca; the sun god Kinich Ahau was usually shown with jaguar features.

facts.label: Palenque
facts.statement: Palenque flourished from 600 to 900 A.D. during the Classic era of the Maya.

facts.label: the Yucatan
facts.statement: The walled city of Tulum and the ruins of Xunantunich in Belize are Maya sites; Yucatec Maya is still spoken on the peninsula.
